def: Computing exact derivatives of a program by applying the chain rule to its recorded elementary operations, neither by small steps nor by symbolic algebra.
A directed acyclic graph whose nodes are values and operations and whose edges are dependencies, recorded as a program runs.
Differentiation that carries a derivative alongside every value, giving the effect of one input on all outputs per pass.
Differentiation that propagates gradients from the output back to the inputs, giving the effect of all inputs on one output per pass.
Pairs of a value and its derivative that obey the product and chain rules, used to implement forward mode.
The derivative of the final output with respect to an intermediate node, stored as its grad in reverse mode.
The backward rule of a tensor operation: from the gradient at its output, compute the gradient at its inputs without building the Jacobian.
The intermediate tensors saved during the forward pass because the backward pass needs them.
Saving activations at only a few layers and recomputing the rest during the backward pass, trading extra compute for memory.
The growth in size of a symbolically differentiated formula, which can be far larger than the original expression.
